prompt: Haskell Ord Double compare NaN result value
answer:
For Haskell’s `Ord Double`, `compare` involving `NaN` returns `GT`:

```haskell
compare NaN NaN  == GT
compare NaN x    == GT
compare x NaN    == GT
```

This is inconsistent with the other comparisons, which all return `False` when either operand is `NaN`:

```haskell
NaN <  x  == False
NaN <= x  == False
NaN >  x  == False
NaN >= x  == False
```

Thus, `Ord Double` does not define a total order for values containing `NaN`; ordered containers using `Double` keys may suffer data loss or corruption. (GHC.Float search result)
